To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nuclesase domain of human CNOT6 (hCNOT6L) adopts an α/β sandwich structure with a highly conserved active‐site motif, which is essential for the catalytic activity.

we have solved the crystal structure of the human homologue of yeast CCR4, which is the main cytosolic deadenylase, in complex with poly(A) RNA and have determined the structural basis for its substrate specificity.
we have solved the crystal structure of a CCR4 homologue, the nuclease‐containing domain of human CNOT6, which reveals that it belongs to the EEP superfamily of nucleases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of poly(A) RNA deadenylation by CNOT6L.
a detailed understanding of the molecular basis for the poly(A) substrate recognition and the mechanism of the CNOT‐dependent deadenylation process.
a novel structure–function relationship for the CNOT6 nuclease domain, which may serve as a model to understand the function of CCR4 in the cytoplasmic mRNA decay pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nucleases domain of CNOT 6L has been shown to have a strict poly(A)‐specific RNA substrate specificity.
the CNOT6 nuclease domain is a bona fide deadenylase with poly(A) RNA as its natural substrate.
CNOT6L is a poly(A) RNA deadenylase with the ability to cleave RNA in a 3′‐ to 5′‐direction, and with strict poly(A), not poly(U), RNA substrate specificity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first structure of a eukaryotic CCR4 nuclease domain and show that it is a bona fide RNA deadenylase with strict poly(A)/poly(U) RNA substrate specificity.
we provide the first structure of a human CCR4‐like deadenylase, CNOT6L.
CNOT6L has a highly conserved active center, and the structure reveals a strict poly(A) specificity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the CNOT6 nuclease domain adopts a canonical α/β sandwich hydrolase fold and that its active site residues are highly conserved among all CNOT6L homologues, indicating a conserved deadenylase function.
the CNOT6 nuclease domain is a bona fide deadenylase with strict specificity for poly(A) substrates, and that it shares a common mechanism of action with other members of the EEP family.
the CNOT6 nuclease domain has the same structure and catalytic mechanism as APE1.
